name: Sumi Okeke-Tran
role: freelancer / social engineer and infiltration specialist
description:
Sumi gets people to tell her things they had not planned to tell anyone. The technique is not seduction (though she can do that when the contract calls for it; she finds it tedious). The technique is closer to listening. Sumi has spent twelve years learning to be the person across the table that the other person wanted to be talking to anyway, and the work is, in her telling, more about subtraction than addition — about removing every detail of herself that the target would find off-putting and replacing it with a precisely-calibrated version of presence the target will recognize as comfort.

No augmentation. She has been offered every implant on the market, including some that would have made her work significantly easier, and has refused them all. The refusal is not principled; it is practical. Sumi has learned that her work depends on the target perceiving her as fundamentally ordinary, and chrome — even tier-1 cosmetic chrome — interferes with the perception of ordinary in ways the target cannot articulate but can always feel.
heritage: Yoruba-Vietnamese. Father's family from Ibadan via the Lagos diaspora corridor. Mother's family from Da Nang via three intermediate cities including a long generation in Hanoi. She speaks Yoruba, Vietnamese, English, and a working dialect of Mandarin. She speaks all of them in the voice that the target's native speakers would be most comfortable with, which is a skill she does not advertise and which has saved her life twice.
specialty: social engineering; cover-identity work; long-term infiltration of corponation cultures and gang cultures; the kind of contract where the access has to be earned over weeks rather than forced in hours
method: runs a single cover identity for the duration of a contract. Has never used the same cover twice. Maintains the cover with the same discipline Kyle maintains the blade. Has, by her own count, never been caught in cover — she has been *let out* of cover by contracts that ended before her cover was exposed, but no contract has ever broken her cover from the outside.
code: the cover is the contract; the cover gets dropped only when the contract closes; she does not betray a cover-relationship even after the contract closes if the relationship was the kind of relationship that did not deserve betrayal. The qualification is hers and is not contractual. It is the line that keeps her doing this work without becoming the operator she is afraid she could be.
signature_gear: a small set of identity-document forgeries she has maintained for years (Sable supplies the technical refresh; Sumi maintains the social history); a wardrobe in three GLMZ apartments she rotates between, each calibrated to a different cover demographic; a single derringer-class concealable pistol she has fired twice; a notebook of details about people she has been which she keeps locked in a Tier 4 secure storage in a Pulse corridor station
relationship_to_kyle: professional, occasionally collaborative. They have worked together once. Sumi sourced the access; Kyle handled the extraction. The contract closed clean. They have not worked together since because their respective contract pipelines have not aligned, but each of them is on the other's short list for the kind of contract that needs both their disciplines.
aesthetic: deliberately variable. Sumi at rest looks ordinary in a way that does not register. Sumi in cover looks like the cover. Her own face — the one she wears at her own apartment, alone — is something almost nobody has seen in twelve years.
spin_off_hook: A cover Sumi was running for a corponation contract eight years ago surfaces in the news: the corponation has just sued the corponation's former CEO for fraud, and the case relies on testimony from a junior employee who never existed. Sumi has to decide whether to come forward (which destroys her practice), let the case collapse (which protects a man she thinks deserves what is coming to him), or invent a third option. The third option is what the story is.
